tool_input.body:
Bead: beadle-4gm1 (P1). Design: `docs/email-payload-handoff.md`, DESIGN.md DES-038.

## Problem

`buildStageContract` wrote the triggering email's body, the stage's call args and the prior stage's output into the ethos mission contract's `context` field. Ethos PR #539 (DES-080) redacts every mission-record writer and has merged. This repo pins ethos v4.16.0, so nothing breaks today, but on the next pin bump a worker reading its own contract would see `[redacted-email]` and scrubbed text, with no error and no failing test.

## Change

- The payload now travels only through the per-spawn, untracked system prompt file (`StagePayload`, `BuildSystemPromptForTools`). The contract carries a fixed reference naming the pipeline and stage. That channel works for a recipe that grants no built-in tools, which a per-stage file or an MCP tool would not.
- Each payload field is fenced with a per-render `crypto/rand` nonce stamped on every daemon-emitted line, including the empty markers, so sender text cannot forge a field boundary. The STAGE INPUT header states the rule.
- Truncation and sanitization state is decided once per field and carried, never re-derived from bytes. The body is sanitized and capped once in `Executor.Run` (`body_truncated` and `body_sanitized` are persisted). `Runner.Run` returns its own truncation state with its output, and the executor carries `pipe`, `pipeTruncated` and `pipeSanitized` as a local set. There is no shared field to reset.
- Arg names are restricted to `^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$` so a name cannot split a fence line.
- Untrusted text (stderr, worker output, validation errors) is capped in logs and errors; a failed temp-file cleanup is surfaced in the returned error; the empty-or-whitespace body decision is logged once.
- `TestClaudeRunner_ContractCarriesNoPayload` drives the real ethos CLI and reads the stored contract back. It accepts `inputs.trigger.from` as either the address or `[redacted-email]`, so it passes on the pinned ethos and on a build with DES-080.

## Verification

- `make check`: lint 0 issues, govulncheck clean, markdownlint clean, `go test -race ./...` passes in every package.
- Real entry point: `TestOnNewMail_EndToEnd` drives the daemon's `OnNewMail` through real trust classification, permission, signature and the real `ethos mission create`, with only the Claude worker faked. 37 tests run verbosely and pass, including the hostile-case fence table, the truncation and sanitization tests through the real stage loop, and the cleanup-failure test. `beadle-daemon` builds and starts.
- Local review: `code-reviewer`, `silent-failure-hunter`, `invariant-completeness-reviewer`, `djb` and `qodo review`. The last round on the fix diff had no findings from either reviewer. Qodo covered the full change with no findings.
- Four implementation missions, two closed failed at a round cap or a write-set boundary, are exported under `.punt-labs/ethos/missions-closed/`.

## Also in this PR

- `.gitignore` no longer ignores `.punt-labs/ethos/sessions/`, so ethos's audit-seal hook can stage its chunks. Three corrupt August chunks were retired with `ethos audit quarantine`.
- The stray `.punt-labs/ethos/ethos.yaml` is removed; the real config is `.punt-labs/ethos.yaml`.

## Demo

The operator confirms the daemon pipeline behavior. No live-mailbox run was done; the end-to-end test is the real-entry-point evidence.

tool_input.prompt:
Review-fix round (T4, no mission) in the main checkout <repo>, branch fix/email-payload-off-contract. You are the only agent working; edit in place. Go. Do not touch .gitignore or .punt-labs/ethos/**. If a commit is blocked by a hook, report the exact error and stop. No git worktree, no push. One commit per finding, staged by file name, each passing `make check` (run it in the background, it takes minutes: `make check > .tmp/chk.log 2>&1; echo "exit $?" >> .tmp/chk.log` then read the log; never run it in the foreground).

Two valid Qodo findings on PR #292:

A. "Binary stage output is corrupted before the next stage." Executor.Run sets `pipe` to the SANITIZED stage result (sanitizeText strips NUL and replaces invalid UTF-8). That `pipe` is also the stdin of the next CLI stage and of the auto-reply (`c.Stdin = strings.NewReader(pipe)`), so a stage that emits binary or non-UTF-8 bytes passes a changed byte stream downstream, while p.Results keeps the raw result. Fix: keep the pipe the executor carries RAW. Sanitize only for display, at the one place the pipe is rendered into the STAGE INPUT fence (ClaudeRunner.Run building StagePayload / fenceField), computing the sanitized flag there from the raw pipe. That makes the sanitization state decided exactly once, at the point of use, and removes pipeSanitized from the Runner.Run signature and the executor's carried set (revert that parameter and the local; keep pipeTruncated). Update all implementors, callers and tests; the existing TestExecutor_SanitizedPipeReachesClaudeStagePayload must still pass (the fence header still says sanitized), and add a test that a CLI stage emitting NUL and \377 passes those exact bytes to the NEXT CLI stage's stdin unchanged.

B. "Reply emails arrive cut off with no warning." runOutput and runCompound used to append the truncation marker when a CLI stage's stdout hit the 1MB cap; they now only return a truncated bool, which only ClaudeRunner shows (in its fence header). In a pipeline whose last stage is a CLI command, the auto-reply and any later CLI stage get cut output with nothing marking it partial. Fix: when the auto-reply stage runs with pipeTruncated true, the executor appends a fixed daemon-authored line to the reply body the sender receives (or, if the reply runner takes the pipe as stdin, to the pipe passed to it only), e.g. "\n[output truncated at 1MB]\n". Do it in Executor.Run at the auto-reply call site, not inside CLIRunner, so the single decision point stays the executor's carried pipeTruncated. Intermediate CLI stages keep the exact bytes. Add a test through the real Executor.Run: a capped CLI stage as the last process stage, then the reply stage's recorded input ends with the notice; and an intermediate capped stage's next CLI stage input does NOT contain the notice.

Report the commit SHAs and the make check result.
